speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-Ray Left Knee: A lytic lesion in the distal femur near the knee joint with a thin rim of bone on the external surface and a 'soap bubble' appearance. Physical Exam: Mild swelling observed around the left knee; tenderness upon palpation without warmth; range of motion limited by pain, particularly on extension and flexion. Special Tests: McMurray, Lachman, and Anterior/Posterior drawer tests are negative. Blood Tests: Complete Blood Count within normal limits, C-Reactive Protein within normal limits, Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate slightly elevated. Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C, Blood Pressure 125/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray shows a lytic lesion with a "soap bubble" appearance in the distal femur, which strongly suggests a Giant Cell Tumor. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out malignancy, I need to see the MRI results for better soft tissue detail. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the left knee. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Left Knee: A lesion in the distal femur with clear demarcation and non-invasive characteristics, suggestive of a benign process.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms a benign, well-demarcated lesion consistent with a Giant Cell Tumor of the distal femur. DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Tumor of the distal femur.
